title: Opaque state tokens and kernel identity values
summary: `StateToken` and `CodeStateToken` are opaque values with `panel()`, `equals()`, versioned `toString()` (`st1.`/`ct1.` + base64url JSON) and `fromString()`, while event and journal payloads keep the `state` object keys of knowledge/contracts#tokens; the system actor type is the reference value `azguard:system`.
why: Public token properties expose storage counters and read-session details that are not a promise (architecture#api-compatibility state evidence); the identities reference fixes the system actor type (D16). Hard risk: the payload serializer must keep the exact `state` keys so events and journal rows have one shape, and cache keys derived from tokens must stay deterministic.

include: `Kernel\Decision\StateToken`, `CodeStateToken`: promoted public properties → private; supported members per knowledge/contracts#tokens; internal readers use `@internal` accessors; `fromString()` rejects unknown version/malformed input with `InvalidIdentityException`

Event envelope (`AccessEvent::toArray()`) builds `state` with the exact keys `kind, storage, panel, incarnation, version, generation, fingerprint` / `kind, panel, build_id, fingerprint` through an internal serializer
All 37 production users of tokens (cache keys, read sessions, Filament if any, explain) switched to supported or `@internal` accessors; I4 entries fixed
Migration lines: token properties → methods; system actor type value
exclude: Ordering or replica-wait semantics for tokens
